name: WhisperLive
description: Collabora's real-time speech-to-text server built on OpenAI Whisper with faster-whisper, TensorRT-LLM, and OpenVINO backends. Streams live microphone or file audio over a WebSocket protocol and returns incremental transcripts. Ships GPU/CPU Docker images. No built-in authentication by default; the listening surface is a raw WebSocket, so it is largely Shodan http.html-blind and routes to Censys/active-probe fingerprinting.
auth_notes: No authentication in the default server (python3 run_server.py). Access control is limited to an optional --cors-origins flag (browser CORS restriction only, not server-side auth) and does not gate non-browser WebSocket clients. The service speaks a custom JSON-over-WebSocket handshake (client sends uid/language/model/task config, server streams segment updates) on port 9090 with no HTML landing page served, so name/title markers do NOT appear in Shodan http.html — fingerprinting relies on port + WebSocket handshake behavior (Censys/active-probe route). A newer OpenAI-compatible REST interface exists but the canonical exposed surface is the 9090 WebSocket.

shodan_dorks.rationale: Port-based: WhisperLive binds 9090 for its WebSocket server; combine with WebSocket product tag to narrow. WhisperLive serves no HTML so http.html dorks return 0 — port + protocol is the reachable signal
A bare HTTP GET to a WebSocket-only endpoint returns 426 Upgrade Required / connection-upgrade headers; on port 9090 this is a strong WhisperLive handshake indicator distinct from generic web servers

WebSocket upgrade headers on 9090 co-occurring with a whisper marker (banner or error body) tightens to WhisperLive vs other 9090 WebSocket services; low volume, high precision. May require Censys/active handshake as Shodan rarely captures the WS body

api_paths: WS / (JSON config handshake: uid, language, task, model, use_vad)
WS streaming: binary PCM audio in / JSON segment transcripts out
GET / (426 Upgrade Required on plain HTTP)
known_vulns: No built-in auth — any WebSocket client that completes the JSON config handshake gets unlimited real-time transcription
GPU compute theft — unauthenticated streaming ASR runs continuously at operator GPU cost with no rate limiting
Audio PII interception surface — live audio streamed to an open endpoint is processed with no consent, auth, or audit logging
--cors-origins provides browser-only protection and does not restrict native/scripted WebSocket clients (false sense of access control)
Model/backend selectable by the client in the handshake (model size, TensorRT/OpenVINO) — client-driven resource selection enables VRAM-exhaustion DoS by requesting the largest model repeatedly
No TLS by default on the WebSocket (ws:// not wss://) — plaintext audio and transcripts on the wire
risk_notes: Primary attack vectors: (1) Compute theft — an open 9090 WebSocket is free real-time GPU transcription, scriptable with the bundled TranscriptionClient. (2) Live audio surveillance/exfil — the endpoint accepts and transcribes streamed audio with no auth; a passive on-path observer also sees plaintext ws:// audio and text. (3) VRAM-exhaustion DoS — the client picks the model size in the handshake, so an attacker forces large-model loads to starve the GPU. (4) Shodan-blindness aids the operator's obscurity but not security — Censys/active WebSocket handshake probing enumerates these hosts where http.html dorks miss them entirely.
deployment_notes: Docker-first: ghcr.io/collabora/whisperlive-gpu (faster-whisper + TensorRT + OpenVINO + ROCm) and ghcr.io/collabora/whisperlive-cpu. Default bind 0.0.0.0:9090, ws:// (no TLS). Backend engine selectable (faster_whisper default, TensorRT-LLM, OpenVINO). Serves NO HTML landing page — Shodan http.html/http.title dorks return 0; this is a Shodan-blind / Censys-and-active-probe platform. Fingerprint by hitting 9090 with a WebSocket upgrade and observing the JSON config handshake, or by the 426 response to a plain HTTP GET. Frequently paired with the WhisperLive browser extension or the collabora/WhisperFusion conversational stack. Common on GPU-as-a-service (Vast.ai, RunPod). No auth means an exposed 9090 is directly usable.
